science.title: Immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic effects of Fasciola hepatica excretory/secretory proteins in a complete Freund’s adjuvant-induced rat model of rheumatoid arthritis
science.description: Helminths can modulate immune responses by suppressing pro-inflammatory Th1/Th17 pathways and enhancing regulatory immunity, offering potential therapeutic benefits in autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study evaluated the anti-arthritic effects of excretory–secretory proteins (ESPs) from Fasciola hepatica in a Complete Freund’s Adjuvant (CFA)-induced RA rat model. Thirty male Wistar rats were assigned to five groups: healthy control, disease control, methotrexate-treated, prophylactic ESP, and therapeutic ESP. Rats in the ESP-treated groups received a cumulative intraperitoneal dose of 0.912 mg of F. hepatica ESPs. Over 28 days, clinical, behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological parameters were assessed. ESP treatment significantly reduced arthritis scores and paw edema (P < 0.05) and alleviated thermal and cold hypersensitivity (P < 0.001). Immunologically, ESP treatment promoted an anti-inflammatory immunoregulatory cytokine profile, characterized by increased interleukin-10 (IL-10) (P < 0.05) and reduced interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) levels (P < 0.01), supporting its proposed immunomodulatory mechanism. In serum, nitric oxide (NO) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were significantly reduced, indicating improved oxidative status, while liver homogenates showed no significant changes for several markers. PET-CT imaging demonstrated reduced inflammatory activity, and histopathological findings confirmed joint protection, with mild hepatic and splenic alterations. These findings indicate that F. hepatica ESPs exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and analgesic effects in experimental RA and may represent a promising immunomodulatory strategy for experimental arthritis, although further mechanistic and safety studies are required.
